items.name: Viasat, Inc.
items.headline: Viasat stockholders elect directors, ratify auditor, approve compensation
whatChanged: Viasat's stockholders elected Mark Dankberg, William LaPlante, and Michael Paull as Class III Directors.
The appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, was ratified.
Stockholders approved, on an advisory basis, the company's executive compensation.
items.decisionTakeaway: The annual meeting results confirm director elections, auditor ratification, and advisory approval of executive compensation, indicating routine governance.

items.name: Ooma, Inc.
items.headline: Ooma Reports Strong Q2 FY2027 Revenue Growth and Profitability Improvement
whatChanged: Total revenue increased 25% year-over-year to $83.2 million for the three months ended July 31, 2026.
Subscription and services revenue grew 24% year-over-year to $75.6 million, driven by Ooma Business and acquisitions.
Product and other revenue increased 46% year-over-year to $7.6 million.
GAAP net income rose to $3.0 million from $1.3 million in the prior year period.
The company prepaid $11.5 million of its term loan borrowings.
items.decisionTakeaway: Ooma demonstrated robust top-line growth and significantly improved profitability in its second fiscal quarter, driven by its business segment and recent acquisitions.

items.name: Grindr Inc.
items.headline: Grindr resolves UK privacy lawsuit for £26 million
whatChanged: Grindr resolved a UK group action related to historical data practices before 2020.
The settlement includes no findings or admission of liability.
Grindr will pay £13.0 million by December 31, 2026, and £13.0 million by March 31, 2027.
The total settlement amount is approximately $17.6 million per payment, based on September 3, 2026 exchange rates.
items.decisionTakeaway: Grindr settled a historical privacy lawsuit for £26 million, impacting future cash flow but resolving a legacy legal issue from a prior ownership period.

items.name: DTE Energy Company
items.headline: DTE Energy Director David A. Thomas to Retire
whatChanged: Director David A. Thomas announced his intent to retire from the Board of Directors.
The retirement is effective September 3, 2026.
Thomas's departure follows 13 years of service.
The retirement is not due to any disagreement with management or the Board.
items.decisionTakeaway: Director David A. Thomas is retiring after 13 years of service, a planned departure without disagreement.

items.name: Crown Holdings, Inc.
items.headline: Crown Holdings Senior VP, General Counsel Adam Dickstein to Retire
whatChanged: Adam Dickstein, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, informed the company of his decision to retire.
His retirement is effective as of December 31, 2026.
This filing reports the planned departure of a key executive.
items.decisionTakeaway: The company announced the upcoming retirement of its Senior Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary, effective at year-end.

items.name: Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
items.headline: Ionis partner Novartis' pelacarsen Phase 3 trial fails primary endpoint
whatChanged: Novartis announced pelacarsen Phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON study did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing cardiovascular events.
Pelacarsen achieved substantially lower Lp(a) levels, consistent with previous studies.
The drug demonstrated an acceptable safety profile.
Full data will be presented at an upcoming medical congress.
items.decisionTakeaway: Ionis' partner Novartis announced a key cardiovascular drug candidate failed to meet its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial, despite lowering Lp(a) levels.

items.name: Matthews International Corporation
items.headline: Matthews International amends loan agreement, releases foreign subsidiary
whatChanged: Ninth amendment to the Third Amended and Restated Loan Agreement executed.
Certain provisions of the Loan Agreement are amended.
Exhibit D to the Loan Agreement is amended.
Schedules 3 and 4 to the Security Agreement are deleted and replaced.
Matthews Europe GmbH is released from the terms and conditions of the Loan Agreement.
items.decisionTakeaway: The company executed a ninth amendment to its loan agreement, which includes releasing a foreign subsidiary from its obligations.

items.name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co.
items.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch Q2 Net Sales Up 5%, Operating Income Rises
whatChanged: Net sales increased 5% year-over-year to $1.27 billion for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026.
Operating income grew 22% year-over-year to $252.7 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026.
Net income attributable to A&F rose 30% year-over-year to $183.7 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026.
The company recognized approximately $100 million in refunds plus $3 million in accrued interest related to IEEPA tariffs previously paid.
Share-based compensation expense decreased slightly to $8.5 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026, from $9.8 million in the prior year period.
items.decisionTakeaway: Abercrombie & Fitch reported a strong second quarter with significant year-over-year growth in net sales, operating income, and net income, bolstered by tariff refunds.
